rows.speaker: عكرمة وعمرو بن فائد
rows.claim: The anomalous nominative reading takes earth as a new clause after a pause at the heavens.
rows.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة عكرمة وعمرو بن فائد والأرض يمرون عليها بالرفع

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī has an anomalous accusative reading for earth.
rows.anchor: وقراءة السدي والأرض نصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative or accusative, pause after the heavens and start a new clause; nominative makes earth the subject, resumed by the pronoun in عليها.
rows.anchor: من رفع أو نصب وقف على السماوات ثم ابتدأ والأرض فالرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative supplies an implicit verb meaning they tread the earth, supported by Ibn Masʿūd's يمشون عليها; the following phrase explains the verb.
rows.anchor: وأما النصب فبفعل مضمر تقديره ويطؤون الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the canonical genitive reading, one may pause after earth or at the end of the verse.
rows.anchor: ومن جر الأرض على قراءة القراء فإن شاء وقف على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥirṣ means striving to attain something; ʿālam means a class of animals capable of knowledge, or the cosmos named in relation to the useful creature for whom it was created.
rows.anchor: الحرص طلب الشيء باجتهاد في إصابته والعالم الجماعة من الحيوان التي من شأنها أن تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāshiya is something that spreads over and envelops; baghtatan is a sudden, unexpected arrival.
rows.anchor: والغاشية المجللة للشيء بانبساطها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʾayyin means kam and derives from ayy with the kāf added; baghtatan is a verbal noun used as a circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: وكأين في معنى كم وأصلها أي دخلت عليها الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding signs should have revealed truth; failure to reflect is the people's fault, since God supplied proofs and the Prophet called them.
rows.anchor: أن التقصير من جهتهم حيث رضوا بالجهل وليس من جهته سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people will not believe despite the Prophet's efforts, because a caller's zeal cannot make an unwilling audience respond.
rows.anchor: وليس أكثر الناس بمصدقين ولو حرصت على إيمانهم وتصديقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no payment for conveying the message, so no fee can deter them from accepting faith.
rows.anchor: ولا تسألهم على تبليغ الرسالة وبيان الشريعة أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is admonition and reminder for all people, not a warning addressed only to this audience.
rows.anchor: ما القرآن إلا موعظة وعبرة وتذكير للخلق أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Countless proofs of God's oneness appear in the heavens and earth, from celestial bodies to mountains, plants, and traces of earlier peoples; disbelievers see them but refuse reflection.
rows.anchor: أي كم من حجة ودلالة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Arab polytheists acknowledged that God created the heavens and earth and sent rain, then associated partners; their talbiya named a partner owned by God along with what it owned.
rows.anchor: إلا شريكا هو لك تملكه وما ملك عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The People of the Book believed in God, the Last Day, Torah, and Gospel but committed shirk by rejecting the Qurʾān and Muhammad's prophethood; the report is transmitted through Dārim b. Qubayṣa from al-Riḍā's forebears to Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: وثالثها: أنهم أهل الكتاب آمنوا بالله واليوم الآخر والتوراة والإنجيل ثم أشركوا بإنكار القرآن وإنكار نبوة نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الحسن

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: The verse may describe hypocrites who display faith while concealing shirk.
rows.anchor: أنهم المنافقون يظهرون الإيمان ويشركون في السر عن البلخي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view says anthropomorphists affirm God generally but associate partners in the details.
rows.anchor: أنهم المشبهة آمنوا في الجملة وأشركوا في التفصيل وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Shirk can mean shirk of obedience: people obey Satan in sins that incur punishment without worshipping another deity.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر ع

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Saying one would have perished or lost one's family but for another person makes that person a partner in God's provision; saying God favored one through that person is acceptable.
rows.anchor: قول الرجل لولا فلان لهلكت ولولا فلان لضاع عيالي

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرضا
rows.claim: Reports identify shirk of blessings; al-Riḍā says it is shirk that does not reach unbelief.
rows.anchor: إنه شرك لا يبلغ به الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The feminine ghāshiya is understood as عقوبة, a punishment enveloping everyone, like a saddle cover.
rows.anchor: على تقدير العقوبة أي عقوبة مجللة لجميعهم عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: The enveloping punishment may be a punishment of annihilation.
rows.anchor: عذاب الاستئصال عن مجاهد وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be lightning and other calamities.
rows.anchor: الصواعق والقوارع عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Hour may suddenly overtake people in their markets, with the cry striking them unaware.
rows.anchor: تهجم الصيحة بالناس وهم في أسواقهم

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads نوحي with first-person nūn; the other readers use third-person يُوحى with an open ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم { إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم } بالنون

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The nūn reading matches إنا أوحينا إليك; the yāʾ reading matches وأوحي إلى نوح and قل أوحي إلي.
rows.anchor: الوجه في النون قوله إنا أوحينا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabīl means a prepared road or route; Islam is a way leading to Paradise. A poem treats sabīl as feminine.
rows.anchor: السبيل الطريق وهو المكان المهيأ للسلوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīra is what enables one to see and know; sayr denotes extended travel in a direction.
rows.anchor: والبصيرة ما يبصر به الشيء أي يعرف

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The Prophet's way is his path, practice, and method.
rows.anchor: أي طريقي وسنتي ومنهاجي عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: مقاتل والجبائي
rows.claim: The phrase may mean the religion and path of the Prophet's call.
rows.anchor: هذه الدعوة التي أدعو إليها ديني وطريقي عن مقاتل والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet calls to God's oneness, justice, and religion with certainty, knowledge, and decisive proof rather than imitation.
rows.anchor: ادعو إلى توحيد الله وعدله ودينه على يقين ومعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his followers call to God, remind people through Qurʾān and admonition, and forbid disobedience.
rows.anchor: { أنا ومن اتبعني } أي أدعوكم أنا ويدعوكم أيضا إليه

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: A grammatical alternative ends the sentence at أدعو إلى الله and starts a new clause, على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: ويجوز أن يتم الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On this syntax, Muhammad's Companions followed the best way.
rows.anchor: يعني أصحاب محمد كانوا على أحسن طريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥān declares God transcendent above the partners ascribed to Him and may be a command to say so or an intervening parenthesis.
rows.anchor: معناه تنزيها لله عما أشركوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet disavows those who set up an equal, spouse, or child alongside God.
rows.anchor: الذين اتخذوا مع الله ندا وكفوا وولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows the merit of calling people to God, His oneness, and justice.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على فضل الدعاء إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report calls scholars trustees of the messengers for God's servants; the passage says the Prophet called to God at all times, while explaining legal rulings at particular times.
rows.anchor: العلماء أمناء الرسل على عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires religious effort to rest on confidence, insight, and decisive proof; this invalidates imitation.
rows.anchor: وفيها دلالة أيضا على أن الواجب في السعي أن يكون على ثقة وبصيرة ودلالة قاطعة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Messengers came from towns because townspeople have more reason and knowledge than desert dwellers, who are far from learning and scholars.
rows.anchor: أرسل الرسل من أهل الأمصار لأنهم أرجح عقلا وعلما من أهل البوادي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ḥasan says no prophet came from the desert, among jinn, or as a woman; desert dwellers tend toward hardness and roughness, while townspeople are sharper.
rows.anchor: لم يبعث الله نبيا قط من أهل البادية ولا من الجن ولا من النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers should travel and consider how God annihilated earlier peoples who rejected their messengers, taking warning from their fate.
rows.anchor: فيعتبروا بهم ويحذروا مثل ما أصابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed believers' enemies and saved them in this world; the Hereafter is better than worldly life and its pleasures.
rows.anchor: إذ أهلكنا عدوهم ونجيناهم من شرهم ولدار الآخرة خير لهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports the Prophet said a span of Paradise is better than the world and everything in it.
rows.anchor: لشبر من الجنة خير من الدنيا وما فيها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains دار الآخرة as the abode of the final state; alternatively, الآخرة modifies دار, while صلاة الأولى may mean the first prayer or first obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: فالآخرة نعت للدار لأن لجميع الخلق دارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفلا تعقلون asks whether they understand what was said and learn from it.
rows.anchor: أي أفلا يفهمون ما قيل لهم فيعلمون

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: The Kufans and Abū Jaʿfar read كذبوا without doubling; the reading is also attributed to ʿAlī, the two Muḥammads, Jaʿfar, Zayd b. ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and al-Aʿmash.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر كذبوا بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: عائشة والحسن وعطاء والزهري وقتادة
rows.claim: These authorities read كذبوا with doubling; Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid are also reported with differing readings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون كذبوا بالتشديد وهي قراءة عائشة والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading has فنجا with one nūn and a light jīm.
rows.anchor: عن ابن محيصن فنجا بفتح النون والجيم والتخفيف

rows.speaker: عيسى الثقفي
rows.claim: ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī reads the three coordinated nouns تصديق, تفصيل, and هدى in the nominative; the standard reading has them accusative.
rows.anchor: ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة برفع الأحرف الثلاثة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With doubled كُذِّبوا, ظنوا refers to the messengers, who knew or thought their peoples had rejected them; this form means being met with denial.
rows.anchor: الضمير في ظنوا في قول من شدد كذبوا للرسل

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With light كَذَبوا, the nations thought the messengers lied; the verb can mean not believing a report and is analogized to ṣadaqa.
rows.anchor: فقال: كذبوا فهو من قولهم كذبتك الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light form would ordinarily take two objects, as ṣadaqa does in the cited verse; poetry also attests forms of كذب.
rows.anchor: أن يتعدى إلى مفعولين كما تعدى صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the light reading, the pronoun may refer to the message recipients, who thought the messengers had lied; this avoids attributing a broken divine promise to the apostles.
rows.anchor: والضمير الذي في قوله { وظنوا أنهم } كذبوا للمرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says the messengers despaired of their people believing, while the people thought the messengers had lied; then God's help came.
rows.anchor: إن الرسل يئسوا من قومهم أن يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present form ننجي narrates a past event as if it were unfolding, as in other Qurʾānic examples.
rows.anchor: فإن ننجي حكاية للحال لأن القصة مما قد مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An active participle loses verbal force when past and specific unless the text narrates a present scene; the dog image is an example of such narration.
rows.anchor: فلولا حكاية الحال لم يعمل اسم الفاعل لأنه إذا مضى اختص

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: The second nūn in ننجي is concealed with jīm; distinct pronunciation is wrong. Nūn assimilates before a close letter, is concealed with non-close oral letters, and is clear before throat letters.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان: تبيينها معها لحن وللنون مع الحروف ثلاث أحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second nūn was likely omitted in writing to avoid identical adjacent letters, as in other spellings; concealment resembles assimilation because the hidden consonant is not distinct.
rows.anchor: كرهوا اجتماع المثلين في الخط حذفوا النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn cannot assimilate into jīm because the letters are neither identical nor close.
rows.anchor: فقد غلط لأنها ليست مثل الجيم ولا مقاربة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single-nūn form فَنُجِّي uses past tense, fitting the past story and its coordination with passive ولا يرد; the active present would pair more naturally with لا نرد.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ فنجي فإنه أتى على لفظ الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading of تصديق supplies a deleted subject, yielding لكن هو تصديق.
rows.anchor: فيكون التقدير لكن هو تصديق الذي بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istayʾasa means despaired as though one sought despair after recognizing impossibility; baʾs is severity or hardship.
rows.anchor: استيأس بمعنى يئس كأنه طلب اليأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣ is a report whose parts follow; ʿibra is an indication leading to an aim, and lubb is the finest part and thus the intellect.
rows.anchor: والقصص الخبر يتلو بعضه بعضا من أخبار من تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage consoles Muhammad: God delayed punishment for earlier deniers as for his people, until the messengers despaired their people would believe, a despair God confirmed.
rows.anchor: إنا أخرنا العقاب عن الأمم السالفة المكذبة لرسلنا

rows.speaker: عائشة والحسن وقتادة وأبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: On the doubled reading, the messengers knew their people had rejected them completely, with no prospect of a believer.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة والحسن وقتادة وأبي علي الجبائي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وابن زيد والضحاك وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: On the light reading, the nations thought the messengers had lied about God's promised victory and destruction of enemies.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility returns the pronoun to the messengers: those who promised faith broke their pledge or lied about their professed faith.
rows.anchor: أن الذين وعدوهم الإيمان من قومهم أخلفوهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: At a gathering, Saʿīd b. Jubayr explained the light reading as recipients thinking the apostles lied; al-Ḍaḥḥāk objected sharply.
rows.anchor: اجتمعا في دعوة فسئل سعيد بن جبير في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Ibn Abī Mulayka says the messengers were human, weakened, despaired, and thought they had been let down, citing متى نصر الله; the author calls this remote.
rows.anchor: قال كانوا بشرا فضعفوا ويئسوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's help came by sending punishment on unbelievers; believers were rescued, while punishment cannot be turned away from polytheist criminals.
rows.anchor: حين يئسوا بإرسال العذاب على الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's story offers reflection: after being thrown into a well, sold, and imprisoned, he became Egypt's ruler and reunited with his family.
rows.anchor: من ملك مصر والجمع بينه وبين أبويه وإخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad had not read books, heard the account, or mixed with its people, yet recounted it with excellent meaning and expression and faced no correction; this supports his truth and prophethood.
rows.anchor: لم يقرأ كتابا ولا سمع حديثا ولا خالط أهله

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: The Qurʾān confirms earlier scriptures because it came as they had foretold.
rows.anchor: لأنه جاء كما بشر به في الكتب عن الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān details what people need of lawful and unlawful matters and Islamic law, and is guidance and mercy benefiting believers in knowledge and practice.
rows.anchor: كل شيء يحتاج إليه من الحلال والحرام وشرائع الإسلام

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads ألا يتخذوا in third person; the rest use second person.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحده ألا يتخذوا بالياء والباقون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ reading follows the preceding third-person wording; the tāʾ reading shifts to direct address, like al-Fātiḥa, although its grammatical addressees remain absent in sense.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالياء فلأن ما تقدمه على لفظ الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥān is an accusative verbal noun meaning I glorify God with glorification.
rows.anchor: سبحان منصوب على المصدر على معنى أسبح لله تسبيحا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Parsing أن لا تتخذوا as indirect quotation is unsound because it is neither a quoted clause nor the meaning of a saying in the relevant construction.
rows.anchor: من زعم أن ألا تتخذوا على إضمار القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible parses make أن purpose-bearing, explanatory (that is, do not take), or extra with an implied command not to take a protector.
rows.anchor: في قوله ألا تتخذوا ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurriya may be an object of اتخاذ with wakīl as second object, a vocative, or a substitute/apposition; singular wakīl can carry collective meaning.
rows.anchor: فإنه يجوز أن يكون مفعول الاتخاذ لأنه فعل يتعدى إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurriya may be raised as a substitute for the subject of تتخذوا, meaning do not take Noah's descendants as a protector, or as an apposition to Banī Isrāʾīl.
rows.anchor: ولو رفع ذرية على البدل من الضمير المرفوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report places the Night Journey in Mecca: Muhammad prayed Maghrib at the Sacred Mosque, traveled that night, and returned at dawn; the destination was Jerusalem as the Qurʾān states.
rows.anchor: نزلت الآية في إسرائه وكان ذلك بمكة صلى المغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the journey occurred only in a dream is false because a dream would provide neither miracle nor proof.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك كان في النوم فظاهر البطلان إذ لا معجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Companion reports of the Ascension fall into four classes: mass-transmitted certainty, rationally possible and accepted as waking, apparently conflicting reports to interpret, and impossible reports without sound interpretation to reject.
rows.anchor: وتقسم جملتها إلى أربعة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey is certain; reports of seeing heavens, prophets, the Throne, Lote Tree, Paradise, and Hell are possible, while seeing people there can mean seeing their descriptions or names.
rows.anchor: فأما الأول المقطوع به فهو أنه أسري به على الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that God spoke face to face, was seen, or sat with the Prophet on a throne imply anthropomorphism; the report of splitting his abdomen is also rejected as unnecessary purification of one already pure.
rows.anchor: كلم الله سبحانه جهرة ورآه وقعد معه على سريره

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Ascension report has Gabriel arrive in Mecca with Michael and Israfil, bring the heavenly Buraq, and carry Muhammad to Jerusalem; the report describes the mount and journey.
rows.anchor: أتاني جبرائيل ع وأنا بمكة فقال قم يا محمد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After prayer in Jerusalem, the Prophet ascends: Jesus and John are in the second heaven, Joseph in the third, Idris in the fourth, Aaron in the fifth, many creatures and cherubim in the sixth, and creatures and angels in the seventh.
rows.anchor: فرأيت فيها عيسى ابن مريم ويحيى بن زكريا ثم صعد بي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra's version places Moses in the sixth heaven and Abraham in the seventh.
rows.anchor: رأيت في السماء السادسة موسى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet went beyond the heavens, saw Paradise, Hell, the Throne, and Lote Tree, returned to Mecca, and was disbelieved when he told people.
rows.anchor: رأيت الجنة والنار ورأيت العرش وسدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: مطعم بن عدي
rows.claim: Muṭʿim b. ʿAdī called the account a lie, challenging Muhammad's claim to have traveled a two-month journey in an hour.
rows.anchor: أتزعم أنك سرت مسيرة شهرين في ساعة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: When Quraysh demanded signs, Muhammad reported drinking and recapping water left by a lost-camel caravan; its owners confirmed the detail.
rows.anchor: مررت بعير بني فلان وقد أضلوا بعيرا لهم وهم في طلبه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: He also predicted that a named person's young camel bolted and broke its hand, which the caravan confirmed.
rows.anchor: مررت بعير بني فلان فنفرت بكرة فلان فانكسرت يدها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: He described Quraysh's Tanʿīm caravan led by a gray camel bearing two sacks, and predicted its arrival at sunrise.
rows.anchor: تقدمها جمل أورق عليه قرارتان محيطتان ويطلع عليكم عند طلوع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people saw the predicted camel arrive but remained unbelieving despite their amazement.
rows.anchor: فبهتوا ولم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In an al-ʿAyyāshī report, angels welcomed Muhammad except Mālik, keeper of Hell; at the Prophet's request Mālik revealed part of Hell, and Muhammad never laughed afterward until death.
rows.anchor: هذا مالك خازن جهنم وهكذا جعله الله

rows.speaker: أبو بصير
rows.claim: Abū Baṣīr reports hearing that Gabriel carried the Prophet to a heavenly place and left him there, saying no prophet had ever set foot there.
rows.anchor: إن جبرائيل احتمل رسول الله حتى انتهى به إلى مكان من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥān declares God free of unsuitable attributes and may express wonder at His power and those who fail to esteem Him; asrā and sarā both mean night travel.
rows.anchor: سبحان كلمة تنزيه وإبراء لله عز اسمه عما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey is said to have occurred one year before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك الليل قبل الهجرة بسنة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators say the journey began at Umm Hāniʾ's house in Mecca, where Muhammad slept; the Sacred Mosque may mean all of Mecca.
rows.anchor: أسري برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من دار أم هانىء

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ḥasan and Qatāda say the journey began inside the Sacred Mosque itself.
rows.anchor: كان الإسراء من نفس المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aqṣā means the farther mosque because of its distance; its surroundings are blessed with vegetation, fruit, security, and fertility.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال الأقصى لبعد المسافة بينه وبين المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another view says its blessing comes from being abode of prophets and place of angelic descent, sanctified from shirk and blessed in religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: جعلناه مقر الأنبياء ومهبط الملائكة عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs shown included the night journey from Mecca, seeing prophets in succession, ascending to heaven, and other wonders.
rows.anchor: ومنها إسراؤه في ليلة واحدة من مكة إلى هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears those affirming or denying the journey and sees the journey and Ascension.
rows.anchor: لأقوال من صدق بذلك أو كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book given to Moses is Torah, guidance and proof for Israel; they were ordered to rely on no protector or lord besides God.
rows.anchor: يعني التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants are the children of those carried with Noah in the Ark and saved from the Flood.
rows.anchor: أولاد من حملنا مع نوح في السفينة فأنجيناه من الطوفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah frequently thanked God, praising Him whenever he dressed, ate, or drank.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا لبس ثوبا أو أكل طعاما أو شرب ماء حمد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Noah said bismillah before eating or drinking and al-ḥamdu lillāh afterward.
rows.anchor: في ابتداء الأكل والشرب بسم الله وفي انتهائه الحمد لله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: The two Imams report Noah's morning and evening gratitude: every religious or worldly blessing came from God alone, whom he praised and thanked until and beyond satisfaction.
rows.anchor: أن ما أصبح أو أمسى بي من نعمة في دين أو دنيا فمنك وحدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One coherence reading links the Moses passage to the Ascension: God showed Muhammad signs as He had shown Moses miracles.
rows.anchor: وأراه الآيات كلها كما أرى موسى الآيات والمعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another link says Muhammad's prophethood was no novelty: God gave him Scripture and proofs as He gave Moses the Torah.
rows.anchor: أن كونك نبيا ليس ببدع فقد آتيناك الكتاب والحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further link says the audience disbelieved in Moses as they rejected the account of Muhammad's Ascension.
rows.anchor: أن معناه أنهم كفروا بموسى كما كفروا

rows.speaker: الشامي والكوفي غير حفص
rows.claim: The Shāmī and Kufan readers except Ḥafṣ read ليسوء with an open hamza; al-Kisāʾī uses nūn and the others read ليسوؤوا with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ليسوء بفتح الهمزة شامي كوفي غير حفص

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās has a noncanonical form of لتفسدن with a ḍamma on tāʾ and fatḥa on sīn; ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī has the reverse vowels.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة ابن عباس لتفسدن بضم التاء وبفتح السين

rows.speaker: علي وأبو السماك وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: ʿAlī reads عبيدا لنا; Abū al-Sammāk reads فحاسوا with ḥāʾ, and Ubayy reads ليسوءا with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقراءة علي ع عبيدا لنا وقراءة أبي السماك فحاسوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For ليسوء, the agent may be God or the earlier sending; God's action may be named although the invaders directly cause distress.
rows.anchor: فاعل ليسوء يجوز أن يكون أحد شيئين إما اسم الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural reading means God sent the invaders to grieve Israel; the repeated بعثناهم is understood, and the invaders grieve by killing and capture.
rows.anchor: بعثناهم ليسوؤوا وجوهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces can stand for their people, as in the cited verses; al-Nābigha's poem uses faces for those attacked.
rows.anchor: الوجوه قد يراد به ذو الوجوه

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ubayy's tanwīn reading may omit a response fāʾ and function as self-command; the later lām forms are commands, and no response to إذا is explicit.
rows.anchor: على حذف الفاء كما يقال إذا سألتني فلأعطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant forms of تفسدن support each other because whoever corrupts also becomes corrupt.
rows.anchor: من أفسد فقد فسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Israel in the Torah that they would twice corrupt their land, identified as Jerusalem, through oppression, taking property, killing prophets, and bloodshed.
rows.anchor: { وقضينا إلى بني إسرائيل } أي أخبرناهم وأعلمناهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وابن زيد
rows.claim: One account identifies the first corruption as killing Zechariah and the second as killing his son John; Sābūr Dhū al-Aktāf and Nebuchadnezzar were sent against them, respectively.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان فسادهم الأول قتل زكريا. والثاني قتل يحيى بن زكريا عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وابن زيد

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq instead says the first corruption was killing Isaiah and the second killing John, while Zechariah died naturally; Nebuchadnezzar and a Babylonian king came against them.
rows.anchor: وقيل الفساد الأول قتل شعيا والثاني قتل يحيى وأن زكريا مات حتف أنفه عن محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies Goliath as the first enemy, defeated by David, and Nebuchadnezzar as the second.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان الأول جالوت فقتله داود ع والثاني بخت نصر عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the verse identifies no specific corruption, so one should not decide among the historical accounts.
rows.anchor: فلا يقطع على شيء مما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel would become greatly arrogant and oppress people; here ʿuluww parallels insolence against God and exposure to His anger.
rows.anchor: والعلو نظير العتو هنا وهو الجرأة على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the first corruption's appointed time, God sent powerful servants against Israel and withdrew His support as recompense for disbelief and rebellion.
rows.anchor: معناه فإذا جاء وقت أولى المرتين اللتين تفسدون فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaḍāʾ means decisive settlement, extending to creation, obligation, or informing; informing is its sense here.
rows.anchor: وبمعنى الإعلام والإخبار بما يكون من الأمر وهو المعنى ها هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUluww means elevation; its verb may mean being able to bear something, rising in virtue, or being high in place.
rows.anchor: والعلو الارتفاع وعلا فلان الشيء إذا أطاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaws means moving through homes and treading them; another gloss is searching thoroughly.
rows.anchor: والجوس التخلل في الديار يقال تركت فلانا يجوس بني فلان

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says a place one enters and treads fits the root.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: كل موضع خالطته ووطئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥassān's poem uses جاس for moving through enemies; another gloss is searching for something thoroughly.
rows.anchor: فجاس به الأعداء عرض العساكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karra means return or political turn; nafīr means the number of men and can denote the clan that supports and goes out with someone.
rows.anchor: والكرة معناه الرجعة والدولة والنفير العدد من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbīr means destruction and tabār ruin; ḥaṣīr means confinement or prison, and also woven reed matting.
rows.anchor: والتتبير الإهلاك والتبار والهلاك والدمار واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labīd's poem illustrates the king called ḥaṣīr.
rows.anchor: جن لدى باب الحصير قيام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ḥasan compares God sending agents against Israel with sending devils against unbelievers to spur them on.
rows.anchor: أرسلنا الشياطين على الكافرين تؤزهم أزا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says God ordered believers to fight Israel.
rows.anchor: أمرنا قوما مؤمنين بقتالكم وجهادكم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim allows that the agents were believers, or unbelievers recruited by a prophet to fight their peers among unbelievers and corrupt people.
rows.anchor: وسلطهم على نظرائهم من الكفار والفساق عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Jāsū through the homes means roaming and searching to see whether anyone remained alive who had not been killed.
rows.anchor: فطافوا وسط الديار يترددون وينظرون هل بقي منهم أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise was certain to occur and could not fail.
rows.anchor: أي موعودا كائنا لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God restored Israel's ascendancy, kingdom, wealth, children, and numerical advantage over its enemies.
rows.anchor: رددنا لكم يا بني إسرائيل الدولة وأظهرناكم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good words and deeds benefit their doers through victory and reward; wrongdoing harms its doers.
rows.anchor: إن أحسنتم في أقوالكم وأفعالكم فنفع إحسانكم عائد عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though فلها can mean فعليها, the author prefers the straightforward sense that harm returns to wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وإذا أمكن حمل الكلام على الظاهر فالأولى أن لا يعدل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may remain to Israel and preserve the sequence, or interrupt the story to exhort Muhammad's community like a preacher's aside.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخطاب لبني إسرائيل ليكون الكلام جاريا على النسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative address, the lesson to Muhammad's community is that good and evil return to oneself, encouraging obedience and warning against sin.
rows.anchor: ومن أساء عاد ضرره إليه ترغيبا وترهيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later promise may mean punishment for the second corruption or the time of that corruption and aggression.
rows.anchor: والمراد به جاء وعد الجزاء على الفساد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invaders grieve Israel by killing and capture; another gloss targets leaders, since humiliating chiefs grieves commoners too.
rows.anchor: بالقتل والأسر يقال سئته أسوءه مساءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosque means Jerusalem's Aqsa; naming the town by its mosque implies the invaders first took control before entering it.
rows.anchor: فكنى بالمسجد وهو المسجد الأقصى عن البلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase as they entered it the first time implies the earlier invaders also entered, though that was not previously stated.
rows.anchor: دل بهذا على أن في المرة الأولى قد دخلوا المسجد أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction covers what the invaders overcame; alternatively, ما with the verb means the duration of their ascendancy, with a genitive element omitted.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما مع الفعل بتأويل المصدر والمضاف محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show Israel mercy after vengeance if they repent and return; renewed corruption brings renewed punishment and subjugation.
rows.anchor: بعد انتقامه منكم إن تبتم ورجعتم إلى طاعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Israel returned to corruption after both episodes, so God sent believers to kill them and take jizya until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: إنهم عادوا بعد الأولى والثانية فسلط الله عليهم المؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Here ḥaṣīr means prison or confinement.
rows.anchor: أي سجنا ومحبسا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A composite account says a Persian or Babylonian king, often Nebuchadnezzar, conquered Jerusalem, destroyed the mosque, burned Torah, polluted it, killed 70,000 over John's blood, and deported captives to Babylon for a century.
rows.anchor: فخرج إليهم وحاصرهم وفتح بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God later sent a Persian king who returned Israel; after a century of obedience they sinned again and the Roman king Antiochus destroyed Jerusalem and captured its people.
rows.anchor: فردهم إلى بيت المقدس فأقاموا به مائة سنة على الطريق المستقيم

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ḥudhayfa says a Roman ruler attacked and captured Israelites.
rows.anchor: غزاهم ملك الرومية وسباهم عن حذيفة

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq traces the first disaster to Israel's sins and says Isaiah advised a king; Isaiah's prayer healed the king and destroyed Sennacherib's forces, leaving five survivors.
rows.anchor: بعث إليهم شعيا قبل مبعث زكريا

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: In Ibn Isḥāq's account, Sennacherib was released and died seven years later; his grandson Nebuchadnezzar ruled, Israel's kingship collapsed, and Israelites fought one another.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر سبحانه بإطلاقه ليخبر قومه بما نزل بهم

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Isaiah preached and fled into a tree when Israel tried to kill him; they sawed it through. God sent Jeremiah, then Nebuchadnezzar entered and exiled them.
rows.anchor: فهرب ودخل شجرة فقطعوا الشجرة بالمنشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says John's murder caused the second disaster: a king wished to marry his wife's daughter, John forbade it, and the girl's mother arranged his death; Nebuchadnezzar killed 70,000 or 72,000 over John's blood, which then stopped flowing.
rows.anchor: إن سبب ذلك كان قتل يحيى بن زكريا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says 210 years separated the two corruptions.
rows.anchor: كان بين الفساد الأول والثاني مائتا سنة وعشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account has Nebuchadnezzar attack first, then Persians and Romans after John's murder, killing 180,000 and destroying the mosque; it remained ruined until ʿUmar rebuilt it.
rows.anchor: إنما غزا بني إسرائيل في المرة الأولى بخت نصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final alternative names Goliath as first invader and Nebuchadnezzar as second; the author concludes God knows best.
rows.anchor: في المرة الأولى جالوت وفي الثانية بخت نصر والله أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubṣira means bright or illuminating. Abū ʿAmr glosses it as a day one sees by; al-Kisāʾī notes usage for daylight, and another reading refers to its inhabitants seeing.
rows.anchor: مبصرة أي مضيئة منيرة نيرة قال أبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muṣḥaf omits the wāw in يدع although it is present in meaning.
rows.anchor: ولا يكتب الواو في يدع في المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative أن after يبشر assumes an omitted bi; the second أن is coordinated, while a new sentence with kasra is possible but unread.
rows.anchor: فتح أن على تقدير حذف الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtadnā derives from aʿdadnā with dāl changed to tāʾ to avoid gemination; كل شيء is governed by an implicit فصلنا clarified by the next verb.
rows.anchor: وأعتدنا أصله أعددنا فقلبت إحدى الدالين تاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān guides to the religion, creed, or path of greatest uprightness.
rows.anchor: يهدي إلى الديانة والملة والطريقة التي هي أشد استقامة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj also glosses it as guidance to the most just word, the confession of oneness, or to the most equitable state: faith in God and messengers and obedience.
rows.anchor: إلى الكلمة التي هي أعدل الكلمات وأصوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do good deeds receive a great reward for obedience.
rows.anchor: ثوابا عظيما على طاعاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those rejecting the afterlife are prepared a painful punishment in Hell.
rows.anchor: { أن الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة } أي بالنشأة الآخرة { اعتدنا لهم } أي هيأنا لهم { عذابا أليما } وهو عذاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment is called ajr because it corresponds to deeds like payment for work; reward is owed by God's gracious commitment even though its benefit returns to the worker.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي العذاب أجرا لأنه يستحق في مقابلة عمل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: People may curse themselves, family, or property in anger as they ask for good; mercy prevents God from granting that destructive request.
rows.anchor: على نفسه وأهله وماله بما لا يحب أن يستجاب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say people may seek evil in haste for benefit or pursue forbidden things as eagerly as permitted ones.
rows.anchor: قد يطلب الشر لاستعجاله المنفعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: People are hasty because they ask for evil as quickly as good.
rows.anchor: يعجل بالدعاء في الشر عجلته بالدعاء في الخير عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another meaning is impatience and inability to bear hardship or ease.
rows.anchor: ضجرا لا صبرا له على ضراء ولا على سراء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report applies haste to Adam: when the spirit reached his navel he tried to rise before able, and humanity shares his haste for things before their time.
rows.anchor: أراد به آدم ع لما انتهت النفخة إلى سرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day show God's oneness through their benefits and alternation; their ending proves they are created and require an omnipotent, knowing creator, beyond human power.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منهما ينقضي لمجيء الآخر وذلك يدل على حدوثهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the two signs as the sun and moon.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الآيتين هنا الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The erased night sign is the moon, whose light was obscured by dark marks; the day sign is the sun.
rows.anchor: وهي القمر أي طمسنا نورها بما جعلنا فيها من السواد عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, night itself is erased and dark like erased writing and day itself is visible; this is an eloquent use of a thing as its own sign.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فتكون آية الليل هي الليل نفسه وآية النهار هي النهار نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says night darkness erases day light and day light erases night darkness, with the second erasure understood.
rows.anchor: فالمراد محونا ظلمة الليل بضوء النهار ومحونا ضوء النهار بظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People rest at night and seek provision by day; the rest clause is omitted here because it occurs elsewhere.
rows.anchor: لتسكنوا بالليل وتطلبوا الرزق بأنواع التصرف في النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day permit calculation of years, months, debts, appointments, lifetimes, and remaining terms; without them nothing could be measured.
rows.anchor: عدد السنين والشهور وآجال الديون وغير ذلك من المواقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguished everything clearly and explained it thoroughly so nothing remains obscure.
rows.anchor: ميزناه تمييزا ظاهرا بينا لا يلتبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may link to God's offer of mercy to Israel: the Qurʾān is the straight path to which they were called to repent and return.
rows.anchor: أمر بني إسرائيل بالرجوع إلى الطريق المستقيم من التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another connection compares Muhammad's upright Qurʾān with Moses's Torah, or links the verse to the preceding Night Journey and its revelation.
rows.anchor: القرآن الذي يهدي إلى الأحسن الأقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning of punishment, the passage says people ignorantly rush to request it; God responds with what benefits them and grants night and day despite their ingratitude.
rows.anchor: مما تقدم من بشارة الكفار بالعذاب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads ويخرج with passive yāʾ; Yaʿqūb reads it with active yāʾ, while the others use nūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ويخرج له بضم الياء وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn ʿĀmir read تُلَقِّيه with tāʾ; the others read يلقاه with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر تلقيه بضم التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On both yāʾ readings, the person's work or fate is brought out or comes out as a book, with كتابا circumstantial.
rows.anchor: فمعناه أنه يخرج له عمله أو يخرج له طائره يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nūn, كتابا is the object, a specification, or a circumstantial phrase meaning accompanied by a book in which deeds are recorded.
rows.anchor: فيكون كتابا مفعولا لنخرج ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منشورا is circumstantial across the readings; yلقاه evokes pages being unfolded, while the alternate phrase is illustrated by a verse about greeting.
rows.anchor: منشورا يكون منصوبا على الحال من الهاء في يلقاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insān is common gender like faras; separate words distinguish male and female animals.
rows.anchor: الإنسان يقع على المذكر والمؤنث فإذا أردت الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basrans derive insān from sociability or humanness on faʿlān; Kufans derive it from forgetfulness, originally insiyān with yāʾ omitted for ease.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق الإنسان من الإنس أو الأنس وهو فعلان عند البصريين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufans cite the diminutive unaysiyān; Basrans treat its yāʾ as extra and the diminutive as irregular, like other listed examples.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا على ذلك بقول العرب في تصغيره إنيسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāʾir means human deeds or fate, likened to an auspicious or inauspicious bird passing right or left.
rows.anchor: والطائر ها هنا عمل الإنسان شبه بالطائر الذي يسنح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sāniḥ moves from one's right to left and is auspicious because a hunter can aim; a bāriḥ crosses the other way and is difficult to aim at.
rows.anchor: والسانح الذي يجعل ميامنه إلى مياسرك والبارح الذي يجعل مياسره

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd says any passing bird, gazelle, or creature is called ṭāʾir; the source begins a poem by Kathīr as evidence but the excerpt ends before its verse.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد ما يجري من طائر أو ظبي أو غيره فهو عندهم طائر
